message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
You can use either:

* the `gcloud` CLI (recommended for quick testing), or  
* the REST API (useful if you’re building a programmatic deployment).

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`).  
> * The Compute Engine API is enabled for that project.  
> * You have a service account key or have authenticated with `gcloud auth login`.  
> * You have the `compute.googleapis.com` scope granted to your service account if you’re calling the REST API directly.  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
    --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
    --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### Optional: Startup script

If you want to install NVIDIA drivers automatically, create a `startup.sh` file:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Reboot to load the driver (optional)
# sudo reboot
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the REST API directly (e.g., from a custom deployment script), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "mode": "READ_WRITE"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### REST API call

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the payload above.

---

## 3. Verify the instance

After creation, you can check the status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=my-gcp-project \
    --zone=us-central1-a
```

Look for the `status` field (`PROVISIONING`, `STAGING`, `RUNNING`, etc.) and the `guestAccelerators` section to confirm the GPU is attached.

---

### Quick checklist

| Step | Command / Action |
|------|------------------|
| 1 | `gcloud config set project my-gcp-project` |
| 2 | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| 3 | Run the `gcloud compute instances create ...` command (or the REST API call) |
| 4 | Verify with `gcloud compute instances describe ...` |

That’s all! Once the instance is `RUNNING`, you can SSH into it and start using the RTX A6000 GPU.
